correctness.rationale: For C f(x)=x^{-1}∫0^x f(t)/(1−t)dt, the coordinate commutator has kernel 1_{t<x}(x−t)/[x(1−t)], bounded by 1 and hence Hilbert–Schmidt. Shifted Jacobi weighted orthogonality and unitary multiplication from L²(x²dx) or L²((1−x)²dx) give two complete orthonormal bases u_n,v_n. Terminating Jacobi hypergeometric coefficients prove ∫0^x(x−t)P_{n−1}^{(2,0)}(2t−1)dt=x² P_{n−1}^{(0,2)}(2x−1)/[n(n+1)] for every n, yielding T v_n=[n(n+1)]⁻¹u_n and the full singular system, not merely a subset. Independently checked this exact integral identity symbolically for n=1,...,6. Telescoping gives trace norm 1, partial fractions give HS²=π²/3−3, and n⁻² singular asymptotics give Schatten p>1/2. Pointwise |T^j f|≤V^j |f| for Volterra integration V and ∥V^j∥≤1/j!, establishing quasinilpotence despite nonzero singular spectrum.
residual_risks: The full-degree polynomial identity relies on the terminating hypergeometric expansion; finite symbolic n≤6 tests are only corroboration.
